The Scroll Container
& the minimal layout engine

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: How a React <Scroll> element becomes a clipped, focusable,

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: D-pad-scrollable viewport on a PlayStation Vita — without a layout engine,

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: except for the one tiny rule it ships with: stack children in a column.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ↑ ↓ D-pad / arrows◀ analog stick⊙ mouse wheel✛ scissor clipping

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: VitaDeck renders React on a QuickJS thread and draws with raylib on the UI thread.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The two meet at a double-buffered instance tree: JS mutates a back buffer,

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: then swaps an immutable snapshot to the front. Scroll position deliberately

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: lives on neither side of that handoff — it is UI-thread state keyed by instance id,

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: so scrolling never round-trips through React.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: QuickJS binding builds an NT_SCROLL node in the back buffer.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Arena-allocated deep copy, swapped in under a mutex after each commit.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Focus, D-pad, analog stick and wheel mutate the scroll-offset map.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Column flow → scissor clip → children → scrollbar → focus ring.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ⟿  scroll offsets survive the swap — the map in scroll.c is keyed by instance id,

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: so a re-render (new snapshot, same ids) keeps your place in the list.

lines.author: matemolnar8
